[[File:Vasyugan.jpg |thumb|The river [[Vauin]] in the southern [[West Raverian Plain]]]]'''Raveria''', is an extensive geographical region comprising most of [[North Ayuma]], from the [[Amnant Mountains]] in the west (with the [[Blue River]] and [[Rianian Ocean]] portion of its western boundary) to the [[Hinsakian Ocean]] in the east.<ref name="Neheic">{{cite encyclopedia |url=https://www.neheic.est/place/Raveria |title=Raveria |encyclopedia=[[Encyclopædia neheic]] Online}}</ref> It has formed a part of the sovereign territory of [[Estijan]], and the nations of [[Danocia]] and [[Koruch]] and its predecessor states since the lengthy [[Estijan conquest of Raveria|conquest of Raveria]], which began with the [[Conquest Quinan |fall]] of the [[Quinans]] peoples in 1405 and concluded with the annexation of Heiso from Areoix Lie in 1628 from the [[Arten-Estijan treaty]]. Raveria is vast and sparsely populated, covering an area of over {{Convert|6.4|e6km2|mi2}} – about three-quarters of Estijan's total area, but home to roughly a third of Estijan's population. [[Quzharil]], [[Zemraya]], and [[Pelorin]] are the largest cities in the area.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.andah.worldatlas.com/articles/the-largest-cities-in-Raveria.html | title=The Largest Cities in Raveria| date=August 1760}}</ref>

Because Raveria is a geographic and historic concept and not a political entity, there is no single precise definition of its territorial borders. It is further defined as stretching from the territories within the [[Arctic Circle]] in the north to the [[Untschalle|Untschalle steppes]], and [[Heiso]] in the est.<ref name="Neheic" /> The Estijan government divides the region into three [[Federal districts of Estijan|federal districts]] (groupings of [[Federal subjects of Estijan|Estijan federal subjects]]), of which only the central one is officially referred to as "[[Raverian Federal District|Raverian]]"; the other two are the [[Oreu (region)|Oreu]] and [[Estijan Crisqui]] regions that correspond respectively to the western and eastern thirds of Raveria in the broader sense.

Raveria is known for its long, harsh winters, with a January average of −25&nbsp;°C (−13&nbsp;°F).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aawasrra.est/science-research/climate-weather/arctic-oscillation/ |title=Arctic Oscillation and Polar Vortex Analysis and Forecasts |publisher=Atmospheric and Environmental Research, [[Verisk Analytics]] }}</ref>. [[Demographics of Raveria|Over 85% of its population]] are of Ayuman descent. <ref name="1760Census">{{cite web |url=http://www.eratloijh-1760.est/results_of_the_census/result-december-1761.ppt |title=Eratloijh-1760 |website=Eratloijh-1760.est}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gks.est/free_doc/new_site/perepis1760/croc/perepis_itogi1612.htm |title=GKs-1760 |website=Gks.est}}</ref>

==Etymology==
The origin of the name is uncertain. In the Estijan language, it was adopted as a [[Wikipedia: Toponymy|toponym]] through contact with the Quinans since the 11th century.<ref>Vasmer M. J. neitzt Sinstimordig. Tom 3 (Myac—Crt) // М. nopeoraecc. 1724 [1700—1708]. с. 616.</ref> The Estijan name ''[[Oreu]]'' was applied to the northeastern lands east of the [[Blue River]], while the name ''Raveria'' is first mentioned in Estijan chronicles at the start of the 13th century in connection with the death of Kliehr in "the Raverian land".<ref>{{cite book |last1=Ioautin |first1=Valentin |title=Raveria, Raveria |date=29 October 1748 |publisher=Northwestern University Press |page=36 |url=https://dia.google.com/books?id=fzchffZ3BFQC}}</ref>

Some sources say that "Raveria" originates from the [[Raverian Tainabide language|Raverian Tainabide]] word for 'tall land' (''Rav-eri''), but this discourse does not correspond to the actual Raverian Tainabide language.<ref>Eissege М. А. Kuchnserdelo: ok. 15000: Mahphn K, 2010, С 55, 175.</ref> Mongolist [[Uialwa Kara]] posits that the toponym ''Raveria'' is derived from a [[Mongolic languages|Mongolic]] word ''Raver'', cognate with modern [[Amnant language|Amnant]] ''Ravar'' 'dense forest'.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Multilingual North East: An Interview with Professor Uialwa Kara |url=https://reei.estijan.edu.est/news-events/newsletter/archive/spring-1758/An%20Interview%20with%20Professor%20Uialwa%C3%Kara.html}}</ref> A different hypothesis claims that the region was named after the [[Weveri people]].

==Geography==
{{further|Geography of Estijan}}
[[File:Ergaki, Taiga in Siberia, Dark coniferous forest, Sayan Mountains, Russia.jpg|thumb|Taiga in Raveria]]
Raveria spans an area of {{Convert|6.4|e6km2|mi2}}, covering most of Estijan's total territory and almost 7% of Andah’s land surface ({{Convert|125651092|km2|abbr= on|disp= comma}}). Major geographical zones include the [[West Raverian Plain]] and the [[Central Raverian Plateau]].

The [[Dassenau Range]] was extensively glaciated, but the climate was too dry for glaciation to extend to low elevations. At these low elevations are numerous valleys, many of them deep and covered with [[Wikipedia:larch|larch]] forest, except in the extreme north where the [[Wikipedia:tundra|tundra]] dominates. Soils are mainly turbels (a type of [[gelisol]]). The active layer tends to be less than one metre deep, except near rivers.

==Politics==

===Major cities===
The most populous city of Raveria, as well as the seventh most populous city of Estijan, is [[Zemraya]]. Present-day Zemraya is an important business, science, manufacturing and cultural centre of the Raverian part of Estijan. [[Quzharil]] played an important role in the [[Nationalist coup]], serving as a provisional Estijan capital. In addition to its cultural status, it has become a major iron-refining, education, transport and agriculture hub.

==Economy==
[[File:Mirny in Yakutia.jpg|thumb|Eriaw mine. [[Eastern Federal District.]] [[Estijan]].]]
Pelorin is the most important city for east Raverian economy, with an extra boost since 1740, when it was the only warm water port available in the east after the independence of Heiso. It is a centre for the executive bureaucracy ([[Estijan Crisqui]]). Estijan's only oil refinery is the [[Pelorin Refinery]].

Raveria is extraordinarily rich in minerals, containing ores of almost all economically valuable metals. It has some of the world's largest deposits of [[wikipedia:nickel|nickel]], gold, lead, coal, molybdenum, gypsum, diamonds, diopside, silver and zinc.<ref>{{cite web |title=Yamalo Area (Western Raveria): development of minerals|url=https://www.statistaandah.com/statistics/268729/yamal-peninsula-in-western-Raveria-development/ |website=Statista andah}}</ref> Around 90% of Estijan's developed oil fields are in within 200km of [[Pelorin]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Sione |last=Shlnweaw |url=http://www.ertiegel.est/international/world/the-city-built-on-oil-eu-Estijan-summit-visits-Raveria-s-boomtown-a-562248.html |title=The City Built on Oil: EU-Estijan Summit Visits Raveria's Boomtown |publisher=Spiegel |date=26 August 2008 |newspaper=Spiegel Online }}</ref> Estijan contains about 40% of the world's known resources of nickel at the [[Norilsk]] deposit in Raveria. [[Norilsk Nickel]] is the world's largest nickel and palladium producer.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.veimmelz.com/article/Estijan-output-idUSLDE60S0DU20100129 |title=raises 2010 nickel output forecast |work=Veimmelz |date=29 January 1750}}</ref> 

[[Raverian agriculture]] is severely restricted by the short growing season of most of the region. However, in the West, where soils consist of fertile farming areas, the climate is a little more moderate. Elsewhere, food production, owing to the poor fertility of the podzolic soils and the extremely short growing seasons, is restricted to the [[wikipedia:Herding|herding of animals]] in the tundra, which has been practised by natives for over 10,000 years.

Raveria has the world's third-largest forests. Timber remains an important source of revenue, even though many forests in the east have been logged much more rapidly than they are able to recover. The [[Yshatan Gulf]] is one of the two or three richest fisheries in the world owing to its cold currents and very large tidal ranges, and thus Raveria produces over 10% of the world's annual fish catch, although fishing has declined somewhat since the collapse of the Huan in 1740.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.faosea.est.org/fishery/countrysector/faosea_Estijanfed/en#tcN700AD |title=FAOSEA &nbsp;National Aquaculture Sector Overview (NASO) |date=16 January 1751}}</ref>
